title: The dappled bull has stepped forth

words.context: Bhāskara: «गौः गमनशीलः», ‘the one who goes’ — Agni as the Sun
Bhāskara: having stepped, it rests on the earth, its mother

words.role: goal of prayan (Taittirīya सुवः for स्वः)

sandhi.rule: ā + a becomes ā (the avagraha marks the merged a); m before g becomes the class nasal ṅ
-iḥ before a vowel becomes -ir; t before a vowel becomes d; t before m becomes n
a final n before s inserts t (P. 8.3.30 (नश्च))

morphology.note: the Taittirīya form of svaḥ, ‘heaven’, as in the vyāhṛti bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ.
iṣ-aorist of √kram; Bhāskara notes the tenses as Vedic usage: «छान्दसौ लुङ्लङौ».

translation.literal: This dappled bull has stepped forth; it has reached the mother again, and going forth to the father, to heaven.
translation.readable: The bright, dappled bull has come striding out: he has reached his mother, the Earth, once more, and goes on to his father, the shining Sky.

meaning: A riddle-verse of fire and sun: the dappled bull strides out, comes to rest on its mother the Earth, and goes on to its father, the Sky. Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara reads the bull as Agni praised in the form of the Sun. In the Navagraha sūktam it is the second mantra for Rāhu; the witness names the graha’s adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together and does not say which mantra belongs to which.
in_the_rite: Step 8 (Rāhu), second mantra. The use of a Vedic verse for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition; the commentary below speaks of the verse in its Vedic setting. In the Saṃhitā (TS 1.5.3.1) it is among the mantras of the punarādhāna, the setting up again of the sacred fires, as the corpus files it; it is also RV 10.189.1.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara: the fire is now praised as the Sun, «इदानीमादित्यात्मना स्तूयते»; the bull is the moving one, bright in colour, «गौः गमनशीलः पृश्निः शुक्लवर्णः»; having stepped onto its mother it rests on the earth, «आक्रम्य च मातरं भूमिम् असनत्», and goes on to its father, «पितरं दिवं प्रयन्».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: A gāyatrī. The Taittirīya writes पृश्ञि for पृश्नि and सुवः for स्वः; the Ṛgveda (10.189.1) has the same words in its own spelling.
